sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Ava Berger
articles.description: The Republican chair of the House Oversight Committee released a scathing report after a 15-month investigation into Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. It faulted the federal government with decades of failing to hold Epstein accountable.
articles.title: Federal government failed to hold Epstein accountable, Republican committee says

articles.author: Jason Breslow
articles.description: House Republicans managed to short-circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort brought against the Defense Secretary by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.
articles.title: House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth

articles.author: Nina Totenberg
articles.description: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.
articles.title: Supreme Court seems split over federal agencies' ability to fine for law violations

articles.author: Charles Maynes
articles.description: Russia's top independent newspaper is closing after more than 30 years amid state pressure and censorship laws. Its founder won the Nobel Peace Prize and several of its journalists have been killed.
articles.title: Russia's most famous independent newspaper has shut down after more than 30 years

articles.author: Alaena Hunt
articles.description: The Rembrandt House Museum in Amsterdam hosted an unusual exhibit in recent weeks — a renowned tattoo artist inking the Dutch master's designs on visitors' skin.
articles.title: Tattoo artists are carrying Rembrandt's art into a new era — and a new medium

articles.author: Halle Zander
articles.description: Drone makers are testing new, big drones that can deliver water or fire retardant with AI assistance. Aspen, Colorado is the first place trying them out. Cool and expensive? Yes. Effective? TBD.
articles.title: Testing the new generation of AI-enabled fire-extinguishing drones

articles.author: Imogen Foulkes
articles.description: The U.S. has skipped a key U.N. human rights review for the second year running. Rights groups warn the absence risks undermining global accountability.
articles.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running

articles.author: Tonya Mosley
articles.description: Mona Chalabi spent five years following Americans living paycheck to paycheck, as well as those earning top wages. Her new book, Ten Lives, explores why financial security can feel so elusive.
articles.title: Americans across the economic spectrum feel a 'panic' about finances, author says

articles.author: Scott Horsley
articles.description: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high.
articles.title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir.
articles.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent

articles.author: Kate Lamb
articles.description:
Capture of man from Java follows reports that hundreds are being recruited from the south-east Asian country as Moscow seeks to boost its war effort
Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation.
The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine captures first Indonesian prisoner of war amid surge in Russian recruitment

articles.author: Kaamil Ahmed
articles.description:
Charities warn of lack of protection amid health fears for more than 940,000 displaced people living in flood-prone areas
Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been left in waterlogged and damaged tents after deadly storms at the weekend, while 150,000 new shelters are held outside Gaza awaiting Israeli approval to enter, aid agencies have said.
At least four Palestinian children and woman were killed as heavy rains and wind battered fragile, leaky tents. Thousands have been left without shelter and sanitation infrastructure has been destroyed, with sewage spewing into people’s tents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands without shelter face lethal conditions in storm-hit Gaza as they wait for 150,000 tents

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Conservationists relocate 3,400 one-flowered wintergreens, a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years
Thousands of one of Britain’s rarest wildflowers have been moved to safety from an eroding Scottish shoreline where they were at risk of falling into the sea.
Conservationists rescued 3,400 one-flowered wintergreen plants at Culbin Forest in Moray, in an effort to protect a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands of rare wildflowers rescued from eroding Scottish coast

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo
articles.description:
Independent Israeli professor says Hussam Abu Safiya’s life will be at risk until he receives proper medical treatment
An independent professor who reviewed the medical records of a prominent Gaza doctor held in an Israeli prison without charge for nearly 23 months has raised serious concerns about his health.
Hussam Abu Safiya was detained at work on 27 December 2024 and later held in solitary confinement at Rakefet, a notorious underground prison.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fresh concerns raised over Gaza doctor held by Israel for 23 months without charge

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy
articles.description:
Three directors were fined a combined $90,000 in federal court judgment and disqualified from managing a corporation for between five and 10 years

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Three directors of a collapsed funeral fund that marketed insurance to Aboriginal families have been banned from managing corporations for at least five years and ordered to pay a combined $90,000 after being found to have breached their duties to clients.
On Wednesday, federal court justice Geoffrey Kennett ordered the former director of the insurance company Youpla Group, previously the Aboriginal Community Benefit Fund (ACBF), Jonathan Law, to pay the commonwealth $50,000 and disqualified him from managing corporations for six years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Youpla directors disqualified over collapsed funeral fund that targeted Aboriginal families

articles.author: Jonathan Barrett and Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Australia’s oldest department store collapsed into voluntary administration last week after years of steep losses

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

David Jones is set to shutter half of its department store network, triggering mass job losses under a sweeping restructure, the appointed receivers said on Wednesday.
David Jones employs more than 6,000 staff across 38 stores.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: David Jones to close half its stores, triggering mass job losses in ‘urgent restructure’

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Three others critically injured and taken to hospitals as reports say car crashed into food stand in North Hollywood
At least three people are dead and three critically injured, after a car struck pedestrians on a Los Angeles corner during Tuesday rush hour, authorities said.
The fatal crash took place near a North Hollywood metro station.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Three dead in Los Angeles after driver crashes into pedestrians, officials say

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Jillian Segal suggested ‘transferring’ powers in updated report released a fortnight ago but government sources note media regulator already exists

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Albanese government won’t follow a suggestion by the antisemitism envoy to scrap the ABC and SBS ombudsmen and replace them with an external oversight body.
In a list of updated priorities released last month, Segal proposed an “external independent ombudsman” to monitor ABC and SBS coverage of the war in Gaza and to ensure publicly funded broadcasters were “held accountable to their own stated standards of accuracy and impartiality”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labor won’t scrap ABC and SBS ombudsmen in favour of external body as suggested by antisemitism envoy

articles.author: Nino Bucci and Jack Larkin
articles.description:
Former CFMEU official Paul Tzimas tells inquiry he suffered fractured ankle and a colleague was left with major injuries and severe PTSD

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former CFMEU official has told a royal commission that underworld figure Mick Gatto attended a meeting that was called after the union official and a colleague were seriously assaulted at a construction site, claiming the underworld figure later offered him a gold bracelet.
Paul Tzimas is the first witness associated with the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union to appear before the royal commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure construction projects in Victoria.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Underworld figure Mick Gatto gave CFMEU official gold bracelet after construction site assault, Big Build royal commission told

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Dave Grohl tells Sydney crowd Russell, whose death was announced this week, was a ‘big’ hero of his

Todd Russell, Beaconsfield mine collapse survivor, dies aged 54 due to illness

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A solemn moment has broken up an otherwise raucous Foo Fighters Australian concert as the band’s frontman made a lengthy on-stage tribute to Beaconsfield survivor Todd Russell.
The US band are touring Australia for the 16th time in their 32-year history and Tuesday night’s Sydney show coincided with the news of Russell’s death at the age of 54.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Foo Fighters interrupt Sydney concert to pay tribute to Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

House Republicans block effort to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth

Sign up for the US Breaking News email


During his press conference, Hegseth was resolute that the articles of impeachment are baseless, and that all attacks were carried out legally.
“As for the articles themselves, Iran, the cartels, Maduro, Yemen, everyone was a lawful operation ordered by the commander-in-chief, then ordered by myself, notified to Congress and executed by American warriors who did their jobs,” he said. “We destroyed terror regimes’ capabilities. We sank the boats carrying poison into our communities. We put a narco dictator in handcuffs. These are not high crimes. This is the job, and it’s the job well done.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon declares ‘total victory’ after House Republicans block effort to impeach Pete Hegseth – as it happened

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
articles.description:
Women are reportedly upstairs neighbors of three Black students, including one who uploaded video to TikTok
Two white students at the University of Mississippi were captured making offensive monkey gestures in a widely panned Ring video that has prompted a school investigation.
On Saturday, freshman Jakiyra Metcalf uploaded the surveillance clip from her apartment door to TikTok, showing one woman thumping her chest and babbling like a monkey. Another woman jumped into the camera’s view and mimicked the primate noises.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two white students at University of Mississippi make monkey gestures in Ring video

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The US actor died in Poland on Tuesday, ‘after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure’, his wife said
Stacy Keach, one of America’s finest stage actors who became best known for playing scruffy private eye Mike Hammer on TV and whose career was nearly derailed after he was imprisoned in 1984 for trying to smuggle cocaine into Britain, has died aged 85.
Keach died at home in Magdalenka, Poland on Tuesday, “after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure,” his wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, said in a statement. Keach had previously suffered a heart attack onstage in Chicago in 2017.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stacy Keach, Mike Hammer actor whose career spanned stage and screen, dies aged 85

articles.author: Abené Clayton
articles.description:
Tech consultant convicted of second-degree murder in 2023 stabbing death of Cash App founder
Nima Momeni, the man convicted of murdering Cash App founder Bob Lee, has been sentenced to 16 years to life.
Momeni, 42, has been in San Francisco’s county jail since late April of 2023, after he was arrested in connection with the stabbing death of Lee, who had created the mobile payment service and was serving as the chief product officer of the cryptocurrency MobileCoin at the time of his death.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nima Momeni sentenced to 16 years to life in murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee

articles.author: Jeremy Barr
articles.description:
Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit
Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. The president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit stems from the BBC’s splicing together of disparate comments he made before the 6 January US Capitol insurrection, as rendered in a Panorama documentary called Trump: A Second Chance.
“Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the Court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” the Trump-appointed Florida district court judge wrote. “It would be difficult for the Court to accept a different framing without completely negating the significance and fragility of political elections.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
Head of major review into adult social care will say that governments have been ‘asleep at the wheel’ of vital system
Successive governments in England have been “asleep at the wheel” on social care, leaving the system to grow as a chaotic patchwork of local services with no clear vision, Louise Casey, the head of the social care commission, is to warn.
Lady Casey, who is preparing proposals for a big review of adult social care, will say the result is that in effect “no one is in charge” of a system that provides vital services for millions of vulnerable people.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No one is in charge’: social care system in England in chaos, Louise Casey to say

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Ombudsman’s report says delays have profound consequences and limit users’ ability to lead independent lives
Disabled people are having to wait up to two years to get a wheelchair because of delays involving NHS bodies and private firms that make them.
The situation is revealed in a report by the parliamentary and health service ombudsman for England, Paula Sussex, who said hold-ups were having profound consequences and limiting wheelchair users’ ability to lead independent lives.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disabled people in England ‘have to wait up to two years for wheelchairs’

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Thinktank Niesr says timid rate rise last week likely to make inflation more persistent feature of UK economy
The Bank of England is risking higher interest rates for longer after a hesitant response to rising inflation, according to leading thinktank.
In a searing critique of the central bank’s tactics, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr) said a timid increase in interest rates last week was likely to mean inflation staying above the Bank’s 2% target until at least 2030.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bank of England’s inflation response ‘risks higher interest rates for longer’

articles.author: Maya Yang and agencies
articles.description:
Estranged father of Duchess of Sussex was arrested for keeping child sexual abuse material, authorities say
The estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, has been jailed after US authorities said he cut an electronic monitoring device off his ankle, days after his arrest for keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units in California.
Thomas Markle, 82, was in custody awaiting a hearing in federal court in Tampa, Florida, first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli said. He was arrested shortly after he cut off the ankle bracelet at 1.45am on Tuesday, Essayli said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, jailed after cutting off ankle monitor, DoJ says

articles.author: David Batty
articles.description:
Arrests made after three properties were searched in relation to inquiry into late businessman
French police have made arrests after raiding three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, in relation to an investigation into sexual abuse and trafficking by Mohamed Al Fayed.
Several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released, according to the Paris public prosecutor’s office. Another property in Paris and one in Saint-Tropez, both with links to Fayed, were also searched in mid-October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: French police raid Ritz hotel in Mohamed Al Fayed sexual abuse investigation

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot has mandate to try to form a government – with Netanyahu waiting if he fails
Opposition lawmakers have wasted no time after Israel’s new Knesset was sworn in, deploying their majority to seize control of the legislature from Benjamin Netanyhau and his allies.
Although they are still too divided to form a government, the opposition requested a vote for a new speaker, who sets the Knesset’s agenda. Once Netanyahu loyalist Amir Ohana has been replaced, the six opposition parties will be able to work on key legislation even if they fail to broker a coalition.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli opposition hurries to seize control as new Knesset is sworn in

articles.author: Daniel Boffey in Hamburg
articles.description:
Countries clash over Sea Lion project as Hamburg tribunal risks deepening sovereignty dispute
The people of the Falkland Islands face “devastating consequences” if Argentina is successful in blocking development of its offshore oilfield, the attorney general for England and Wales has told an international tribunal.
Ellie Reeves, representing the British government at a hearing of the international tribunal for the law of the sea (Itlos), said billions of pounds vital to the future of the British overseas territory would be lost.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Falkland Islanders face ‘devastating consequences’ if Argentina blocks oil project, says UK

articles.author: Sally Weale and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Hamish Falconer says UK has ‘not accepted principle’ of linking electricity trade to ‘cohesion fund’ but two sides will discuss issue
Britain is willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity market, according to the minister in charge of renegotiating the bilateral relationship.
Hamish Falconer, the cabinet minister in charge of EU talks, told the Guardian he was sure the two sides would discuss the issue after this month’s summit, as ministers look to deepen ties with the union over the next few years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Britain willing to discuss paying into EU to join electricity market, says minister

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh in Oslo
articles.description:
New alliance with the Netherlands and Baltic and Nordic countries comes in response to 41% increase in Russian naval activity around UK
Russian naval activity around the UK has increased by 41% in the first nine months of the year, a British defence minister has said, as the Royal Navy announced plans to step up a 10-country maritime defensive effort in response.
Luke Pollard, the minister for defence readiness, described the figure as “a huge increase”, justifying a new drone and warship initiative from “the alliance of beer-drinking nations” – the UK, the Netherlands and the Baltic and Nordic countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russian naval aggression prompts new defensive initiative with ‘beer-drinking nations’

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now); Yohannes Lowe and Martin Belam (earlier)
articles.description:
US-led talks in Abu Dhabi break up after four hours but are expected to resume tomorrow as Zelenskyy says humanitarian issues were discussed

US officials seek ‘final end’ to Russia-Ukraine war as talks begin

The EU has said it stands ready “to come with a swift and united response” after France blamed Iran for a spate of cyber-attacks on supermarket freezers and chillers that caused millions of euros of damage.
Speaking to journalists on Monday, French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said “Europe-wide sanctions” would be imposed against those responsible as he announced France believed that Iran’s Revolutionary Guards were “responsible for this attack”.
We acknowledge that France has attributed these (cyber-attacks) to Iran. Pending discussions with member states, we as (the) European Union, we stand ready to come with a swift and united response.
We as the EU, we have consistently called on all states to refrain from malicious behaviour in the cyberspace. And we will continue to address such malicious behavior, making use of all the tools that we have also under the EU cyber diplomacy toolbox, including sanctions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia-Ukraine talks ‘very productive,’ says US’s Rubio – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press at the Rafah crossing
articles.description:
Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent
Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.
The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities

articles.author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya and Rebecca Bailey
articles.description:
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’

Cop31 live – latest updates

China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.
As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising
Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.
Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.
The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi, and you can read an excerpt from the book here.)
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison Chief Middle East correspondent
articles.description:
Opposition politicians get first chance to take control of levers of power, even as they struggle to form government
Israel’s new Knesset will be sworn in on Tuesday, giving opposition politicians their first chance to take control of some levers of power, even as they struggle to form a new government to unseat Benjamin Netanyahu.
High on the agenda will be replacing the speaker, who wields immense influence by controlling the legislature’s agenda and committee chairs. The current speaker is Amir Ohana, a close ally of Netanyahu.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Knesset speaker could be key to ousting Netanyahu as Israel’s PM

articles.author: Andrew Roth in Washington
articles.description:
President, after talks with Qatari PM, suggests end to war coming ‘fairly soon’ and military escalation not needed
Donald Trump has said that the war in Iran is “effectively over” as he played down concerns that the US would escalate its military campaign against Tehran after the midterm elections.
During a White House press conference, Trump said that Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and that an escalation was not needed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump says US war in Iran ‘effectively over’ as he plays down escalation concerns

articles.author: Oliver Wyndham-Lewis and Magdalena Shopova for the MetDesk
articles.description:
Violent storms lash northern Iraq and parts of Iran, while Portugal faces strong winds and Japan braces for further snowfall
Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms swept across the region, including in neighbouring Iran. The city of Erbil, in Iraq, was particularly badly hit, with extensive damage to homes and businesses. Streets were inundated as torrential rain fell over a short period.
Rainfall exceeded forecasts, with an estimated 80mm falling in the city, compared with expectations of 30mm. Two people were killed in the floods.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Deadly floods hit Iraq as thunderstorms sweep across region

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Pontiff tells Argentina’s president the economy must benefit all on second stop of 12-day Latin America tour
Pope Leo XIV has delivered a stinging critique of Argentine president Javier Milei’s harsh austerity measures, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause in Buenos Aires.
“The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy,” he said on Sunday, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pope Leo delivers stinging rebuke of Milei’s austerity measures during Argentina visit

articles.author: Marina Dunbar and Robert Mackey
articles.description:
CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing
Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.
The New York Times reported in ​October that Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives
African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.
See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester

articles.author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires
articles.description:
President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’
Trees are being planted in the garden. The brightly coloured buildings are getting another coat of paint. The choir rehearses. Hundreds of other residents, several of them using wheelchairs, practise their positions outside the sanctuary. Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina.
But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities. Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event
Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.
High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body. In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis

articles.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe, Gloria Dickie and Elisângela Mendonça
articles.description:
Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo
The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.
A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm

articles.author: Amy Hawkins
articles.description:
Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minority
The deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back.
Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men to China despite pleas from the men themselves and the UN.
 

 

 The US and Canada had reportedly offered to resettle them, but Bangkok appeared to want to avoid upsetting Beijing. The UN has said the returnees’ whereabouts remain unknown.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Uyghurs facing deportation by Thailand say they will be ‘like slaves’ in China

articles.author: Eva Corlett in Auckland
articles.description:
National party will be largest in parliament but ultimate shape of next government won’t be settled for some time
New Zealand could be facing a weeks-long wait to know the shape of its next government, after its nail-biting election failed to hand a decisive victory to either the incumbent rightwing coalition or opposition left bloc.
On preliminary results, the centre-right National party, led by the prime minister, Christopher Luxon, managed to secure enough seats to govern alongside its traditional coalition partners, the libertarian Act and populist New Zealand First parties.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NZ election 2026: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty with results ‘too close to call’

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result
The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.
Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.
Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield, Elisângela Mendonça and Phoebe Weston and Spoorthy Raman
articles.description:
Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of  Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports

British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.
This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

House Republicans block effort to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth

Sign up for the US Breaking News email


During his press conference, Hegseth was resolute that the articles of impeachment are baseless, and that all attacks were carried out legally.
“As for the articles themselves, Iran, the cartels, Maduro, Yemen, everyone was a lawful operation ordered by the commander-in-chief, then ordered by myself, notified to Congress and executed by American warriors who did their jobs,” he said. “We destroyed terror regimes’ capabilities. We sank the boats carrying poison into our communities. We put a narco dictator in handcuffs. These are not high crimes. This is the job, and it’s the job well done.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon declares ‘total victory’ after House Republicans block effort to impeach Pete Hegseth – as it happened

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Republicans in the US House of Representatives banded together on Tuesday, 10 November, to derail an effort to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth. The chamber voted 211 to 204 in favor of a motion to refer the impeachment charges to the Republican-led House judiciary committee, effectively stopping the effort to impeach Hegseth sponsored by Kentucky Republican representative Thomas Massie

House Republicans block effort to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth

 Continue reading...
articles.title: US House votes to derail impeachment of Pete Hegseth – video

articles.author: Jeremy Barr
articles.description:
Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit
Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. The president’s $10bn defamation lawsuit stems from the BBC’s splicing together of disparate comments he made before the 6 January US Capitol insurrection, as rendered in a Panorama documentary called Trump: A Second Chance.
“Accepting the allegations in the complaint as true, the Court finds Trump plausibly pled damages where Trump alleges a defamatory documentary released toward the election caused reputational harm,” the Trump-appointed Florida district court judge wrote. “It would be difficult for the Court to accept a different framing without completely negating the significance and fragility of political elections.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Trump ally, accused of an array of illegal acts, had earlier condemned impeachment push as ‘a farce and a stunt’
House Republicans on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Pete Hegseth, rejecting allegations that the defense secretary had repeatedly violated the constitution through his handling of the Iran war and other conflicts globally.
The vote came a week after Republicans lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives in their worst midterm election in more than a half century, and underscored how lawmakers remain wary of crossing Donald Trump, who has signaled his continued support for Hegseth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House Republicans block effort to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Controversial far-right congressman defied 2022 subpoena from Capitol attack panel and was accused of ignoring sexual abuse as college wrestling coach
The election of Jim Jordan on Tuesday to lead House Republicans elevates a combative Donald Trump ideologue who defied a congressional subpoena over the 6 January attack, as the party tries as it tries to adjust to life out of power.
Jordan will lead a diminished Republican conference, as its ranks shrink to one of the smallest in decades. But it is a triumph for the Ohio Republican who was pushed out of the contentious House speakership race three years ago after his Republican colleagues repeatedly voted against his bid for the gavel in the chaotic aftermath of Kevin McCarthy’s ouster.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Who is Jim Jordan? Pugnacious Trump ideologue to lead diminished Republican ranks

articles.description:
New York senator Chuck Schumer expressed confidence that he would become the majority leader after the Democratic party gained at least 54 seats in the Senate during the midterm elections. Schumer's remarks came after Vermont senator Bernie Sanders announced he would not support Schumer for the leadership position. Sanders joins a growing list of Democratic senators who have said they will not support Schumer
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Schumer confident on Senate leadership role despite dwindling votes – video

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Republicans pick Jordan as House leader and John Thune as Senate leader for last two years of Trump’s presidency

US politics – live updates

Republicans have elected veteran congressman Jim Jordan as their new leader in the House of Representatives, putting a strident defender of Donald Trump at the helm of their conference as they navigate the fallout from sweeping losses in last week’s midterm elections.
Jordan will serve as minority leader under the new Congress that begins next year, where Democrats will have their largest margins in both the House and Senate in years. He will be responsible for shaping the party’s strategy against the waves of investigations Democrats have promised to open into Trump’s second administration, as well as their vows of an ambitious legislative agenda, regardless of whether it has the president’s support.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republicans elect Jim Jordan as House minority leader after midterm defeats

articles.description:
Pete Hegseth said moves to impeach him over alleged abuse of power in the Iran war were 'a farce' that would fail. The US defence secretary was speaking a day after Thomas Massie, Kentucky's Republican representative, introduced eight articles of impeachment against him


US politics: latest updates

 Continue reading...
articles.title: 'It's a farce': Pete Hegseth dismisses impeachment effort against him – video

articles.author: Martin Pengelly
articles.description:
The veteran journalist’s Crossing the Rubicon comes after a historic election where Democrats took over state legislatures across the US
Mark Danner’s new book, Crossing the Rubicon, collects his writing on politics for the New York Review of Books over the quarter-century since Bush v Gore in 2000. It arrives in the aftermath of another momentous election, the midterms tsunami that swamped Donald Trump and his Republican party and will give Democrats control of Congress next year.
From January, battle will commence between Congress and a lame duck president. Democrats have two years to hold the president accountable and build a case to take back the White House and to address damage done by the depredations of Elon Musk and Doge, by budget chief Russell Vought, and by other destructive forces.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The path is very difficult’: Mark Danner on why Democrats shouldn’t aim to only rebuild post-midterms

articles.author: Anna Louie Sussman
articles.description:
Canada, the Netherlands and Sweden offer extra support to solo-parent households. In its latest pronatalist push, the Trump administration aims to shift funds away from them
When news broke that the Trump administration planned to pay married couples to have one parent stay home with their kids, everyone from policy wonks to Redditors bemoaned what they saw as a new front in the mommy wars.
The proposal would shift funds that subsidize childcare for low-income working parents – the majority of them single parents who rely on childcare providers – to low-income married couples with one earner. Given that most single parents and stay-at-home parents are women, and both groups would be applying for the same limited funds, it seemed almost designed to pit moms against each other.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A Trump proposal would punish single parents. Other wealthy countries have a different approach

articles.author: Kenneth Roth
articles.description:
Congressional investigations are only part of the solution. A civic project will do needed legal legwork
The Democrats’ midterm victory was resounding, but it will not be enough to re-establish the rule of law in the United States.
The basic principle that even the president and his officials and cronies are subject to the law has been profoundly undermined by Donald Trump through unchecked ICE violence, apparently large-scale official corruption, and frequent defiance of the law.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump-era lawlessness must be prosecuted. Our new group is working to end the impunity | Kenneth Roth

articles.author: Naomi Klein
articles.description:
If Democrats want to keep the blue wave going into 2028, they have to take on the billionaire class 
Welcome back to How We Win, a Guardian opinion series with leading thinkers, offering bold ideas for America’s political future. Last week, Judd Legum shined a spotlight on the role of dark money in US elections. Today’s edition was written by Naomi Klein, Guardian US columnist and author of End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World, co-written with Astra Taylor.
To see the battle lines of the post-midterm era in sharp relief, look to Texas.
The oligarchs in this battle seem to have no loyalty to the nations, states and cities that helped them grow their enormous wealth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The many v the money’ should frame the next US Congress

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
The potential presidential contender has misread the electorate – and that’s just the start of his problems
The good news is that the dramatic results of last week’s midterm elections mean that Donald Trump and his administration will be much less able to immiserate and impoverish the American people for the next two years, that newly competitive states are likely to see an influx of investment from Democrats, and that states that were once under seemingly unbreakable regimes of Republican control now have Democratic state governments that will hopefully pursue more just, or at least less cruel, policy agendas.
The bad news is that the 2028 presidential cycle has already begun.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: JD Vance’s first 2028 pitch reveals his profound weakness as a candidate | Moira Donegan

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
With weeks left on the congressional calendar, House and Senate representatives have a host of issues they still need to tackle
On their first day back in the Capitol after comprehensive defeats in last week’s midterm elections, Republicans were divided into two camps: those who saw the catastrophe coming, and those who did not.
“I told you exactly what was going to happen. Over and over and over, I told you,” said West Virginia senator Jim Justice. “I said really and truly, if you weren’t concerned and you were a Republican, you were living in a cave. That was my exact words.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republicans return to Washington to sift through wreckage of midterms rout

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright with Moustafa Bayoumi . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Monica Espitia, engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
In an interview this week, Donald Trump was asked to give his assessment of why Republicans lost so badly in the midterms. Along with gas prices, the president blamed 'a dislike for Israel' among voters. It’s an acknowledgment that might not be made by some senior figures in the Democratic party. For years, there have been calls for them to change their stance on Israel, and now those calls are coming from newly elected members in the House and Senate. Kai Wright speaks to Moustafa Bayoumi about why the fight over Israel in the Democratic party is just beginning, and what an influx of lawmakers winning on pro-Palestine platforms means for the future of Aipac


There is a showdown looming in the Democratic party over support for Israel

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries have an Israel problem – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Stephen Miller is an ideologue on a mission to reshape the world. But his appointment has a silver lining for Democrats
Has the midterms bloodbath made Donald Trump go all woke? Has his party’s historic rebuke finally made him reflect on his actions and forced a road to Damascus moment?
Of course not; this is the world’s least introspective man we are talking about. However, for about 30 seconds on Sunday, the usually incoherent president managed the amazing feat of speaking a little bit of sense.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: We have a new shadow president – and he can play Trump like a fiddle | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Late-night host discussed the defense secretary’s  attacks on DEI, time as a Fox News host and ties to nationalist groups
On his HBO show on Sunday night, John Oliver focused on Pete Hegseth, characterizing his actions as secretary of war as “taking a wrecking ball” to the US military.
Oliver described Hegseth as “the guy you constantly see trying to show off by publicly exercising with troops and recruits, and to go by fitness experts on the internet, not doing a great job of it”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: John Oliver on Pete Hegseth’s military plans: ‘Dr Seuss for concussed bigots’

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Conservationists relocate 3,400 one-flowered wintergreens, a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years
Thousands of one of Britain’s rarest wildflowers have been moved to safety from an eroding Scottish shoreline where they were at risk of falling into the sea.
Conservationists rescued 3,400 one-flowered wintergreen plants at Culbin Forest in Moray, in an effort to protect a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands of rare wildflowers rescued from eroding Scottish coast

articles.author: Jeremy Barr

Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit
Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case. articles.title: Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
Head of major review into adult social care will say that governments have been ‘asleep at the wheel’ of vital system
Successive governments in England have been “asleep at the wheel” on social care, leaving the system to grow as a chaotic patchwork of local services with no clear vision, Louise Casey, the head of the social care commission, is to warn.
Lady Casey, who is preparing proposals for a big review of adult social care, will say the result is that in effect “no one is in charge” of a system that provides vital services for millions of vulnerable people.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No one is in charge’: social care system in England in chaos, Louise Casey to say

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Ombudsman’s report says delays have profound consequences and limit users’ ability to lead independent lives
Disabled people are having to wait up to two years to get a wheelchair because of delays involving NHS bodies and private firms that make them.
The situation is revealed in a report by the parliamentary and health service ombudsman for England, Paula Sussex, who said hold-ups were having profound consequences and limiting wheelchair users’ ability to lead independent lives.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disabled people in England ‘have to wait up to two years for wheelchairs’

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Thinktank Niesr says timid rate rise last week likely to make inflation more persistent feature of UK economy
The Bank of England is risking higher interest rates for longer after a hesitant response to rising inflation, according to leading thinktank.
In a searing critique of the central bank’s tactics, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr) said a timid increase in interest rates last week was likely to mean inflation staying above the Bank’s 2% target until at least 2030.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bank of England’s inflation response ‘risks higher interest rates for longer’

articles.author: Maya Yang and agencies
articles.description:
Estranged father of Duchess of Sussex was arrested for keeping child sexual abuse material, authorities say
The estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, has been jailed after US authorities said he cut an electronic monitoring device off his ankle, days after his arrest for keeping child sexual abuse material in storage units in California.
Thomas Markle, 82, was in custody awaiting a hearing in federal court in Tampa, Florida, first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli said. He was arrested shortly after he cut off the ankle bracelet at 1.45am on Tuesday, Essayli said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, jailed after cutting off ankle monitor, DoJ says

articles.author: Andrew Roth in Washington
articles.description:
New indictment claims Mohammad Dawood al-Saadi, a dual Iranian and Iraqi national, plotted while in US custody
US federal prosecutors have said that an Iranian operative jailed in New York was responsible for the foiled attack on a UK air force base where American B-1 bombers were stationed.
A new indictment alleged that Mohammad Dawood al-Saadi, a dual Iranian and Iraqi national, plotted while in custody and then transmitted plans – using coded messages in calls to his family – to two co-conspirators to buy large quantities of chemicals that could be used as explosives in an attack on the RAF Fairford base in September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US prosecutors charge Iranian operative allegedly responsible for UK air force base attack

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Man, 41, arrested near Gloucester by police working with US authorities in investigation involving ‘allegations of espionage’, according to FBI director
A US soldier with alleged links to Russia has been arrested by British counter-terrorism police.
The man, 41, was arrested as part of an investigation by counter-terrorism police, working closely with US authorities, the US military and the FBI, London counter-terrorism police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK counter-terrorism police arrest senior US soldier with alleged links to Russia

articles.author: David Batty
articles.description:
Arrests made after three properties were searched in relation to inquiry into late businessman
French police have made arrests after raiding three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, in relation to an investigation into sexual abuse and trafficking by Mohamed Al Fayed.
Several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released, according to the Paris public prosecutor’s office. Another property in Paris and one in Saint-Tropez, both with links to Fayed, were also searched in mid-October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: French police raid Ritz hotel in Mohamed Al Fayed sexual abuse investigation

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
The key task should be to ensure that essential services improve the wellbeing  of individuals and local communities, writes Peter Riddle. Plus letters from Sheila Triggs and Stephen Smith
A key lesson for the UK from the US midterm elections is that a different approach to managing the economy is essential if Labour hopes to retain power in two years’ time. Voters in the UK will judge Andy Burnham’s government just as harshly as American voters have judged Donald Trump if they too feel the economy is not working for them.
Meeting the rising costs of food, utilities, transport and housing has become a daily challenge for millions of people. The pain of rising costs is compounded by a collapse in the quality and reliability of many vital public services and a sense that many people feel that their community life has become more fractious, fragile and unsafe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Growth at all costs is not a sustainable policy | Letters

articles.author: Sally Weale and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Hamish Falconer says UK has ‘not accepted principle’ of linking electricity trade to ‘cohesion fund’ but two sides will discuss issue
Britain is willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity market, according to the minister in charge of renegotiating the bilateral relationship.
Hamish Falconer, the cabinet minister in charge of EU talks, told the Guardian he was sure the two sides would discuss the issue after this month’s summit, as ministers look to deepen ties with the union over the next few years.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Britain willing to discuss paying into EU to join electricity market, says minister

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
Conservative leader launches Welfare That Works policy document outlining benefit reductions of £36bn
Badenoch and Whately are now taking questions.
Q: [From Rob Powell from Sky News] We are running a report on the Netherlands, where youth unemployment is much lower than in the UK, but the amount they spend on getting people into work is much higher. Do you want to spend more on job training and support?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Planned Tory welfare cuts ‘a charter for human misery,’ says Labour – as it happened

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Premature death risk also varies according to employment and qualifications, shows analysis ‘laying bare the scale of inequalities’
People living in the most deprived areas of England are more than twice as likely to die prematurely than their more affluent counterparts, according to analysis.
The research, conducted by the Health Foundation, took demographic data from the 2021 census to look at differences in premature mortality rates – defined as any adult who died before their 75th birthday – alongside further data on deaths from March 2021 to December 2023.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: People in deprived areas of England more than twice as likely to die early, study shows

articles.author: Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
Host Turkey celebrates new oilfields as UN climate summit prepares to host world leaders from more than 90 countries
We’ve just heard from Patricia Espinosa, the former UN climate boss (succeeded by Simon Stiell) and now we are hearing from former US secretary of state and climate ambassador, John Kerry.
Kerry has congratulated Brazil for keeping the fossil fuel transition issue alive, and the room has erupted in cheers.

Multiple women allege David Walliams abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were young women, an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News has found. He denies the allegations. Maeve McClenaghan reports
David Walliams, the comedian and former Britain’s Got Talent judge, is alleged to have groomed fans he met when they were as young as 15. Walliams denies any wrongdoing.
In this episode, investigations correspondent Maeve McClenaghan tells Nosheen Iqbal about the investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.
You can watch this podcast on YouTube.
The ITV News documentary David Walliams: Power and Silence is available to watch on YouTube and ITVX.

articles.title: The allegations against David Walliams - podcast

articles.author: Michael Savage , Emine Sinmaz and Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Met says several people have been in contact since start of disgraced comedian’s rape and sexual assault trial

Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault

Police have received further criminal allegations against Russell Brand since the start of his trial.
The Metropolitan police said several people had been in contact during and since the conclusion of the 51-year-old’s rape and sexual assault case.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police receive further criminal allegations against Russell Brand

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
GLP-1 products such as Ozempic and Mounjaro spread but many in poorer countries struggle to get basic diabetes treatment
The gold rush into GLP-1 weight-loss drugs risks diverting pharmaceutical firms’ attention away from diabetes treatments such as insulin, the head of the Access to Medicine Foundation has warned.
GLP-1 blockbuster medications such as Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro have revolutionised obesity and diabetes treatment but there has been a greater focus by companies on weight loss, according to a report from the Netherlands-based non-profit group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pharma firms’ focus on weight-loss drugs could put insulin supply at risk, experts warn

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Maeve McClenaghan . Video produced by James Tindale & Eleanor Biggs . Sound design by Eli Block . Motion graphics by Natalie Gegan . Executive produced by Homa Khaleeli, Elizabeth Cassin, Phil Maynard & Rachel Oldroyd
articles.description:
Multiple women allege David Walliams abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were young women, an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News has found. He denies the allegations.

In a letter addressed to journalists working on this investigation, Walliams writes: 'Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

'I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.'

He adds: 'I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.'
 Continue reading...

Comedian and former Britain’s Got Talent judge alleged to have groomed fans he met when they were as young as 15 and harassed women in the workplace over a number of years. He denies the allegations

articles.author: Guardian community team
articles.description:
We’d like to hear from retail workers about their experiences of abuse, threats and violence at work
More than half of UK shop workers face abuse or attacks from customers every week, according to new research by the charity Retail Trust. The figure has risen from 33% to 54% in just two years, prompting calls for shoppers to show greater respect ahead of the upcoming busy Christmas period.
We’d like to hear from retail workers about their experiences. Have you faced verbal abuse, threats or physical violence from customers or have you been filmed without your consent?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shop workers in the UK: have you experienced abuse from customers?

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes
Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”.
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Shoppers appear to have taken government’s Be Ready campaign seriously, retail analysts say
British shoppers have been stocking up on essentials such as bottled water, tinned goods and hand sanitiser, but did not panic buy after the government advised people to prepare for emergencies, shopping data has shown.
Sales of essentials jumped in the 10 days after the government launched its Be Ready campaign, which encourages households to prepare for up to three days in the event of disruption to essential services from incidents such as cyber-attacks or extreme weather.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Britons stockpiling water and food tins but not panic buying, figures show

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Iran war has fuelled energy price rise and clouded outlook, driving up unemployment, says Clare Lombardelli
Young people in Britain are bearing the brunt of a “low-gear economy” as employers hold back from hiring amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East, a deputy governor of the Bank of England has warned.
Clare Lombardelli, the Bank’s deputy governor for monetary policy, said the unfolding conflict, which has triggered a surge in energy prices and clouded the outlook for the economy, was contributing to an increase in youth unemployment.

articles.author: Lana Crowe
articles.description:
As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost
A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids. That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm, citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”.
The current canary in the coalmine however is the storyboard artist, whose work gen AI appears to have directly in its sights. Storyboard artists are the illustrators who draw the panels of images with notes and diagrams that map out scenes before they are filmed. Storyboards are used to work out how a film will look, and as a blueprint to communicate a director’s vision to cast and crew, and are one of the first steps in bringing a script off the page. Now they appear on the verge of replacement by programmes that use text prompts to create illustrations instead. Even an old-school diehard like Martin Scorsese has got on board; in June he announced a partnership with an AI firm whose text-to-image model he used in the storyboarding process for his next movie.

These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. You don’t even have to get out of bed to start playing. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Earlier this year, I was stuck in hospital for several days, fuzzy on pain medication and bored out of my mind, with nothing but a Steam Deck for company. In the middle of one of those long nights, unable to sleep, I played a game called Titanium Court. It’s a strange creation that looks like it was made for the ZX Spectrum and reads like a postmodern Shakespeare adaptation – a compelling mix of strategy game and match-3 where you rearrange battlefields by matching tiles, before sending tiny lo-fi fairy armies to their deaths.
At the end of this late-night run, I met a boss I’d defeated before – a comically hungry dragon – and the game asked if I would like to skip the boss fight and enjoy a musical performance instead. A game has never asked me this before. Of course, I accepted. And then, instead of the familiar tiled battlefield, I was looking at a pixellated singer-songwriter, who launched into an extremely long preamble about the mating habits of the Pacific salmon before saying, “This is a song for anyone else who ever got so horny they could die,” and launching into a soulful acoustic guitar number accompanied by crude images of leaping fish. I began to wonder if my meds were making me hallucinate.
